findings.issue: מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה places the ash outside the camp (min + outside, relative to the camp). "a fuera al campamento" turns min into motion toward and reads the camp as the destination.
נִדָּה is a common noun, not a proper name; "nidá" leaves the lemma untranslated.
Unmarked "la" resumes the ash as object of the second verb. Hebrew has no second object pronoun; same referent, grammatical smoothing.

notes: Remaining clauses track the tokens, including verbless חַטָּאת הִוא as "pecado ella."
